current_f2_context.broker_authority: PerceptionCaptureBroker remains one-owner bounded admission/drop authority
current_f2_context.temporal_authority: captured_monotonic_ns plus existing clock calibration/uncertainty rules
current_f2_context.acceptance_state_observed: WP714 preparation has resolved listed WP708/WP710/WP711/WP712/WP713 repository-CI dependencies; final Perception Fabric acceptance still requires a non-synthetic local real-device/OS-permission receipt

mapped_policy.name: BROWSER_RENDERED_CAPABILITY_NEGOTIATED_CAPTURE/v1
startup: bind exact browser build/version and CDP protocol identity
discover/verify whether Page.startScreencast and required parameters are actually supported on that exact protocol
never infer tip-of-tree experimental capability from browser family/name alone
mapped_policy.continuous_preferred_candidate: Page.startScreencast only when exact capability/version acceptance passes
mapped_policy.on_demand_candidate: Page.captureScreenshot for explicit high-fidelity/specific-region evidence when required
screencast_flow_control: use positive bounded maxFramesInFlight; exact value is a measured configuration, not a source-derived constant
validate/hash/map frame provenance and publish to the existing local broker before acknowledging the CDP frame
acknowledgement must not wait for downstream semantic/model consumption because that would turn CDP transport flow control into a second perception scheduling/admission authority
broker queue/drop counters remain the canonical local overload evidence
sendLastFrame remains measurement-gated because the protocol explicitly describes a performance-versus-latency trade
mapped_policy.timestamp_rule: Page.screencastFrame.metadata.timestamp (Network.TimeSinceEpoch) is auxiliary browser clock data only. F2 captures local captured_monotonic_ns on receipt/admission and may map the browser timestamp only through existing clock-domain calibration/uncertainty machinery.
mapped_policy.generation_rule: navigation, target replacement, detach/reconnect or invalidating protocol restart advances source_generation/epoch before new rendered observations rejoin fusion.

expected_benefit: Preserves a continuous event-stream option with explicit transport backpressure while retaining a broadly compatible pull fallback, without changing F2 capture ownership or temporal authority.
counterhypotheses: Sampled captureScreenshot may be cheaper and sufficient for actual workloads, making screencast unnecessary complexity.
Experimental startScreencast may fail compatibility/reconnect tests frequently enough that it should not be preferred even when present.
Acknowledging immediately after local broker publication may still permit excess encode/network work if broker is dropping heavily; scheduler/cadence adaptation may need to reduce screencast rate.
Browser TimeSinceEpoch may be too unstable or low-value to calibrate; dropping it while retaining local monotonic receipt time may be simpler.
required_measurements: CPU/RSS and encoded bytes per second
broker accepted/dropped counts versus maxFramesInFlight/everyNthFrame settings
screenshot pull cadence cost at matched effective observation rate
browser-epoch to local-monotonic calibration stability if browser timestamp is retained
next_discriminator: E3/E4 on exact target browser/runtime comparing bounded screencast and sampled screenshot under matched observation workloads. No runtime/physical/efficiency credit before those measurements and the owner-authorized local acceptance boundary.
